name: São Tomé and Príncipe
official: Democratic Republic of São Tomé and Príncipe

facts.religion: Catholic about 55%, Protestant and other Christian

snapshot: Africa's second-smallest country, two cocoa islands in the Gulf of Guinea, where governments often fall but power changes without bloodshed.
culture: The uninhabited islands were settled by the Portuguese with enslaved Africans to grow sugar, and later cocoa on vast plantations called roças, many now crumbling or turned into hotels. Forro and other creoles are spoken alongside Portuguese. The Tchiloli, a 16th-century European drama performed in masks and costume, has become a uniquely São Toméan art form.
society: Cocoa remains the main export, and tourism is growing slowly. The state relies heavily on foreign aid. Hopes of offshore oil have repeatedly faded. Political rivalry is intense: President Carlos Vila Nova sacked Prime Minister Patrice Trovoada in January 2025.
baseline: After dismissing Trovoada's government, Vila Nova appointed Américo Ramos as prime minister. A 2022 attack on the army headquarters, in which detainees were killed in custody, remains a source of political tension.

leaders.gov: Prime Minister Américo Ramos, since January 2025
